A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiaBlo research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiaBlo experiments on reasoning, code generation, safety alignment, quantized models, and training runtime, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains original DiaBlo experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, sparsity comparisons, gradient measurements, and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The procedure remains zero-initialized, additive block-diagonal adaptation with frozen pretrained weights and batched block computations. v2 clarifies padding and truncation for nondivisible dimensions, an already stated capability. The additional quantizers, models, and restricted-update experiments do not introduce a new DiaBlo component.

E1.justification: v2 adds instruction-following training on WizardLM with first-turn MT-Bench evaluation, and natural-language-understanding evaluations on MRPC, CoLA, SST-2, QNLI, and MNLI from GLUE (Appendices A.3.2–A.3.3). These substantially broaden task coverage. The original reasoning, code-generation, and safety datasets remain; BF16 commonsense evaluation moves to the appendix.

E2.justification: v2 adds full-fine-tuning and zero-shot controls to existing benchmark comparisons, MagR-LoRA to the 2-bit comparison, and four random sparsity patterns in Table 5. LoRA-GA becomes an evaluated comparator on MT-Bench. The unquantized LoRA reference row from v1 Table 5 is removed from the corresponding quantization table. Renaming DiaBlo to MagR-DiaBlo does not constitute a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds model configurations including Llama-13B, Llama2-13B, Llama3.2-3B, and T5-base; GPTQ quantization controls; GPT-4 judging for MT-Bench; GLUE development-set evaluation; and controlled sparsity and sensitivity protocols. For existing Llama3-8B CodeAlpaca training at N=128, the reported learning rate changes from 5e-5 to 3e-5 and the scheduler from linear to constant (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 15). This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing whether that experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct tests of diagonal versus random sparsity patterns, controls separating quantizer effects from adaptation effects, activation/output-gradient rank measurements, and gradient-norm diagnostics. Appendices A.3.4–A.3.7 add optimization-stability, block-count, learning-rate, module-selection, and layer-sensitivity analyses. These substantially expand the evidence explaining when and why DiaBlo works.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, benchmark confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 Table 9 measures gradient-norm variance across training steps as an optimization diagnostic, rather than uncertainty in performance estimates. The 95% effective-rank threshold likewise is not a confidence interval.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for larger models, quantization controls, diagnostic analyses, MT-Bench (6.26), and GLUE (87.8 average). Llama3-8B DiaBlo at N=64 changes its reported HumanEval Pass@1/5/10 from 41.8/56.4/62.9 to 43.2/57.4/63.5 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 3), while v1's additional-epoch results disappear. Most original scores remain, including the relocated BF16 results; the 170/480-minute runtime findings are retained in prose.

T1.justification: v1 provides gradient identities and computational-complexity arguments but no sufficiency theorems. v2 Section 3.2 and Appendix A.1 add least-squares and full-objective stationarity results under generic low-rank assumptions, a supporting Kronecker-product rank lemma, and proofs. The general theorem establishes a conditional implication from block stationarity to full-weight stationarity.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion add theoretical guarantees as a central contribution: greater expressivity than LoRA in the linear setting under parameter constraints, and claimed convergence to full-fine-tuning stationary points under low-rank conditions. v1 primarily claims empirical effectiveness, stable optimization, and efficiency, without these formal guarantees.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's geometric intuition and unresolved theoretical explanation with a low-rank sufficiency interpretation. It newly attributes quantized-model gains primarily to DiaBlo, explains diagonal sparsity advantages, and interprets block-count saturation and stronger early/middle-layer adaptability. The explicit v1 limitations section, including the acknowledgment that non-language modalities remain untested, is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds exact model-loading identifiers and non-instruction-tuned status (Table 11), explicit padding/truncation instructions, hyperparameters for MT-Bench, GLUE, and sparse GSM8K experiments (Tables 18–20), and retained-update scaling factors. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's original experiment settings. The code repository address is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning beyond the existing LoRA and SMT discussion to random masking, sparse random adaptation, S2FT, and SparseLoRA, emphasizing structured sparsity and hardware efficiency. It also adds low-rank activation/gradient and mathematical references supporting the new theoretical comparison, plus sources for the added benchmarks. This is substantive positioning expansion rather than merely the switch to author-year citations.

P1.justification: v2 substantially revises the introduction, contribution list, and conclusion around theoretical sufficiency and sparse adaptation. It reorganizes Section 3.2, moves BF16 commonsense discussion into Appendix A.3.1, converts the runtime table discussion into prose, and restructures the appendix into proofs, validation, additional experiments, and implementation details. The limitations section is replaced by different end matter, including a reproducibility statement.

P2.justification: v2 adds a benchmark-summary chart and new rank, gradient, learning-rate, module, and layer plots (Figures 2–7), together with new benchmark and diagnostic tables. Existing tables gain model panels and control rows. The BF16 table moves to the appendix, while the runtime table is replaced by prose retaining its findings. Conference formatting also changes the page layout.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly leaves diagonal adaptation's effectiveness theoretically unexplained and provides limited direct testing of the diagonal-block choice. v2 substantially strengthens that central argument through conditional proofs, matched sparsity comparisons, quantizer controls, and sensitivity studies. The broader benchmarks and implementation details add useful support. Qualifications remain: the general theorem assumes stationarity rather than proving training convergence, and the explicit limitations discussion disappears. These weaknesses temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in justification and diagnostic evidence.
